walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK imports roughly 46% of its food — high food miles raise CO2.

Agribusiness in East Anglia uses big machines, pesticides and irrigation — efficient but environmentally damaging.

Local trends: farmers' markets, allotments, seasonal eating reduce food miles.

Rainfall is uneven: wet NW (Lake District) vs dry SE (London region).

Water transfer: schemes like Kielder Reservoir in Northumberland supply NE England.

Demand is high in the south-east — population dense and gardens water-thirsty. Climate change makes droughts more likely.

The UK has shifted away from coal:

Gas ~40%, renewables (mostly wind) ~40%+, nuclear ~15%, coal ~1%.

Trade-offs: fracking is controversial; wind is variable; nuclear is low-carbon but expensive and produces waste.

mcqs.q: Why is a food web a better model than a food chain?
options: A food web is the same as a food chain, just drawn differently.
A food web shows what spiders eat and a food chain shows what other animals eat.
A food chain shows one linear path; a food web shows the many interconnected feeding relationships in reality, so it better represents how species depend on multiple food sources.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.

mcqs.q: What does a 'large scale' map mean?
options: A large-scale map shows a large area.
Large scale means the map is physically big.
A large-scale map covers a small area in high detail (e.g. 1:25,000 OS map of one town); a small-scale map covers a large area in less detail (e.g. 1:1,000,000 world atlas).
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes of similar magnitude cause different amounts of damage?
options: All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
Large scale means the map is physically big.
Bigger magnitude always means more deaths.
Damage depends on depth, distance from population, building quality, ground type (liquefaction risk), time of day, and emergency preparedness — not just magnitude.
